subsystems.name: Reactive tool tip
subsystems.role: the working end that picks up, holds and deposits individual atoms or small molecular groups.
parts: a few reactive atoms (e.g. a dangling bond or carbide group)

subsystems.name: Positioning mechanism
subsystems.role: moves the tip to a chosen atomic site with sub-nanometre precision.
parts: piezoelectric actuators or a molecular-scale gantry

subsystems.name: Feedstock handling
subsystems.role: supplies the atoms or molecules being assembled and keeps them from reacting at the wrong time.

subsystems.name: Control and programming
subsystems.role: translates a design into a sequence of pick-and-place instructions and checks each one worked.

subsystems.name: Rigid scaffold
subsystems.role: a stiff frame holding many tips in fixed register — proposed to be built from diamond-like carbon.
parts: anchoring points for tips and wires

subsystems.name: Power and environment
subsystems.role: delivers energy and heat removal; most candidate chemistry needs vacuum and often low temperature.
parts: local energy source (chemical, optical or electrical)

buildSteps.title: Prove single-bond mechanosynthesis
buildSteps.detail: Using a scanning probe tip, force a specific bond to form between two chosen molecules — the most basic act of positional assembly. A handful of such reactions have been driven with atomic force microscopes.

buildSteps.title: Design a selective tip
buildSteps.detail: Work out by computation which tip chemistry will pick up the intended fragment, hold it, place it, and then let go without disturbing neighbouring bonds.

buildSteps.title: Build a molecular positioning stage
buildSteps.detail: Scale the proven probe platform down and stiffen it, so a tip can be stepped from one lattice site to the next and stop there repeatably.

buildSteps.title: Make storable feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Synthesise small molecules that are stable in a bottle but reactive once presented at the tip, so the machine has something to build with.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a small atomically precise part
buildSteps.detail: Use the tip to build a modest structure — a few dozen atoms in an exact pattern — and verify it, proving the loop of place, check, continue.

buildSteps.title: Parallelise for throughput
buildSteps.detail: One tip is hopelessly slow. Build arrays of tips working at once, plus rapid automated inspection, to reach useful production rates.

buildSteps.title: Lift to larger building blocks
buildSteps.detail: Once small parts can be made reliably, use them as components to assemble bigger structural units — the route from molecular parts to visible objects.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap better machines
buildSteps.detail: Use early machines to build improved machines, including the stiff diamond-like scaffolds and fine tips needed for general-purpose manufacturing.

prerequisites.why: individual atoms have been moved and a few bonds made deliberately, but only one at a time and in special conditions.
the ribosome is an existing proof that a machine can build precise molecular products from a programmed sequence — it just cannot make arbitrary materials.
bottom-up chemistry already makes exact structures such as graphene nanoribbons, but the range is narrow.
a useful assembler must find and fix its own mistakes, and no such autonomous system exists.

prerequisites.tech: Simulation of reaction pathways at surfaces
prerequisites.why: tip chemistry must be predicted before it is attempted; current models are useful but not fully predictive.

pathway.milestone: probe-based chemistry on single molecules, plus bottom-up synthesis of exact nanostructures
pathway.unlocks: evidence that atoms can be placed where we want them.

pathway.milestone: a machine that repeatedly builds a defined atomically precise product without human intervention
pathway.unlocks: the first real assembler, however slow and narrow.

pathway.milestone: stiff scaffolds with thousands of parallel tips
pathway.unlocks: output high enough to matter for materials and electronics.

pathway.milestone: machines that build copies of themselves from simple feedstock
general-purpose positional manufacturing of bulk materials
pathway.unlocks: products with strength, precision and cleanliness no conventional factory can match.
